Group: issue #1 alone. No duplicates exist in this one-issue batch.

Verdict: easy-call. Medium difficulty, narrow query pagination regression investigation and fix; no public API or schema change is needed.

Verified against 14f32ec5d5df1e70f7c138b243e097bfdfb6d034: CollectionFetchPaginationQueryTransformer detaches fetched plural joins, including plural fetches nested under fetched singulars, and reattaches them outside the paginated derived table. Its absorption collector traverses selections, sort expressions, and moved join predicates, but not the WHERE predicate. BaseSqmToSqlAstConverter.canPushPaginationDown guards plural-fetch ordering but has no analogous WHERE-path guard. SelectionQueryImpl.isPaginationPushedToDerivedTable mirrors the converter preconditions and must stay consistent with any fallback change. These source facts support the fetched-child-alias failure hypothesis, but do not constitute a runtime reproduction.

Relevant files: hibernate-core/src/main/java/org/hibernate/query/sqm/sql/spi/BaseSqmToSqlAstConverter.java; hibernate-core/src/main/java/org/hibernate/query/internal/SelectionQueryImpl.java; hibernate-core/src/test/java/org/hibernate/orm/test/pagination/CollectionFetchPaginationTest.java. The transformer is in query/sqm/sql/internal/CollectionFetchPaginationQueryTransformer.java.

Two-way door: an internal guard/fallback with regression tests is reversible and need not change public contracts.

Implementation: first add a small regression test for filtering on a fetched collection alias with stable ordering and nonzero offset, alongside an unpaginated control. Confirm the intended SQL alias failure in Actions before changing production code. If confirmed, use the existing in-memory pagination fallback for unsafe references, keeping converter and runtime decisions synchronized. Do not merely move WHERE outside the paginated query. Retain optimized SQL pagination for safe independent non-fetch joins. Existing nonFetchJoinPlusFetchJoin tests already cover an association-join predicate staying inner; the reported ad-hoc Flag join still needs its own regression control and may already work at this revision.

Open questions: exact current-main behavior for both reported query shapes; correlated predicate/subquery path scope; preservation of filtered fetched-collection semantics and offset/limit results.
